gaps.sentence: A true friend will always ___ a secret.
gaps.explanation: keep a secret is the fixed collocation for not telling it to anyone.

gaps.sentence: Please ___ sure that all the windows are locked.
gaps.explanation: make sure means to check that something is true or has been done.

gaps.sentence: She always ___ her best, even in friendly matches.
gaps.explanation: do one's best means to try as hard as possible; the -es form agrees with 'she'.

gaps.sentence: The wedding will ___ place in the village church.
gaps.explanation: take place means to happen; it is the fixed phrase for events.

gaps.sentence: She has ___ great progress since she changed schools.
gaps.explanation: make progress is the collocation; after 'has' the past participle 'made' is needed.

gaps.sentence: He didn't ___ any interest in politics until university.
gaps.explanation: take an interest in something means to become curious or involved in it.

gaps.sentence: She was bitterly ___ when her proposal was rejected.
gaps.hint: adjective collocating with 'bitterly' after bad news
gaps.explanation: bitterly disappointed is the standard collocation; 'bitterly' combines with negative feelings.

gaps.sentence: The roads were almost empty — the traffic was surprisingly ___.
gaps.explanation: light traffic means few vehicles on the road; its opposite is heavy traffic.
